note: Seven bench tests that turn the simulation's assumptions into measurements. Each has a target from the finite element model; enter a result to see whether the design window still holds.

tests.name: Wet silicone on silicone friction
tests.why: Sets whether womb pulses can slip the baby through the sleeve. The model stalls at 0.8.
tests.kit: Two cast sheets (Dragon Skin 10 NV and Ecoflex 00-30), a tilting board with a protractor, water, a 200 g sled.
steps: Clamp the Ecoflex sheet to the board and wet it.
Wrap the sled in Dragon Skin 10 NV, place it on the sheet.
Tilt slowly until the sled slides; record the angle. Repeat 10 times.
Static friction = tan(angle). Repeat with a drop of dish soap in the water.
source: ASTM D1894, coefficient of friction of plastic film

tests.name: Yield stress of the gel bath
tests.why: Decides whether the folded baby can break out of the gel by buoyancy and the arm's help.
tests.kit: The real Carbomer 940 bath, a set of steel balls (3 to 12 mm), a ruler, a timer.
steps: Fill a tall jar with the bath, let it settle 1 hour.
Drop balls from small to large; note the largest that stays held for 60 s.
Convert the largest held ball to a yield stress with the critical yield number for a sphere in Beris et al. (1985), or measure directly on a rheometer if one is available.
tests.target: 40 Pa or less with the arm assisting, or deepen the bed
source: Beris et al. 1985, sphere in a Bingham plastic, J. Fluid Mech. 158

tests.name: Breakout pull of a printed folded disc
tests.why: The real risk in the model: the baby must leave the gel without tearing.
tests.kit: One printed and cured folded disc (D 210, 6 pleats) in the bath, a luggage scale, a hook through the needle valve.
steps: Print the disc at the real depth (58 mm under the surface) and cure.
Pull straight up slowly with the scale; record the peak force.
Repeat with the bed 100 and 120 mm deep.
source: Hajash et al. 2017, Large-Scale Rapid Liquid Printing

tests.name: Bellows pressure, volume and outer radius
tests.why: Checks the bulging point near 1.5 kPa and the length growth used in the model.
tests.kit: A printed bellows, a water manometer (clear tube and ruler), a 60 ml syringe or the pump, calipers.
steps: Seal the bellows on the needle valve; connect the manometer.
Add air in 0.5 L steps; at each step record pressure (mm of water, 1 mm = 9.8 Pa), length and outer radius.
Stop at 1.5 kPa or at the tether.
source: Mooney 1940, A theory of large elastic deformation, J. Appl. Phys. 11

tests.name: Sleeve pull through and seal pressure
tests.why: Sets the sleeve radius: the model wants r 80 to 85 mm.
tests.kit: Sleeves cast at r 80, 85 and 90 mm, the inflated bellows, a luggage scale, the manometer.
steps: Pull the inflated bellows through each wet sleeve; record the peak force.
Close one end, pressurise the other side; record the pressure where air leaks past the bellows.
tests.target: pull 12 to 20 N, seal at least 0.7 kPa

tests.name: Pump flow into the closed womb
tests.why: The push is limited by flow: about 2 mm/s of growth at 3 L/min.
tests.kit: The pump, the sealed mother with snorkel, the manometer, a 10 L bag.
steps: Measure free flow by filling the bag; time it.
Close the womb; record the time to reach 0.7 kPa and the flow at that pressure.

tests.name: Opening force of the canal lips
tests.why: The push leaves about 7 N for the lips to open.
tests.kit: The printed lips, a rod with a rounded end of D 210, a luggage scale.
steps: Wet the lips; push the rod through slowly.
